- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent sentiment spikes (especially +1.00s) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate downward moves when sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.33 or 0.67) — model ignores or delays reaction to bearish signals.
- Model overreacts to recent price volatility — forecasts show excessive lag or overshoot after sharp moves (e.g., 85+ → 70+).
- Mean reversion bias: model holds too much upward momentum even when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — prices often revert to 75–80 range after 82+ peaks.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., 82+ → 80+), especially when sentiment is mixed or mildly bearish.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67), model tends to overfit recent highs — fails to account for eventual pullback or consolidation.
- Model underweights sentiment in early periods — forecasts remain high even when sentiment is weak or negative, suggesting lagged sentiment integration.
